prompt: Match each role to what it delivers.
hint: Name each by what it hands to somebody else.

pairs.right: Data that arrives correct and on time
The recurring answer and its written definition
An answer to a new question, with its doubts
A model that predicts or decides

prompt: What does the lesson say is wrong with picturing the four roles as a ladder, analyst at the bottom and data scientist at the top?
hint: Kind or rank?

choices.text: The ladder runs the other way: analysts are the senior role
choices.why: Reversing the ladder keeps the mistake; the roles are not ranked at all.

choices.text: The roles differ in kind, and seniority exists inside each one
choices.why: Right: each answers a different question, and seniority exists inside each.

choices.text: Data engineers belong at the top because the others depend on them
choices.why: Dependence is not rank; the lesson rejects any ordering of the four.

choices.text: Nothing; it is how careers in data progress
choices.why: The lesson calls that picture wrong in its first paragraph.

prompt: Lívia's analysis of why October fell turns out to be wanted every month. What does the lesson say happens to it?
hint: Once, then again.

choices.text: It goes to the data scientist, since repetition calls for a model
choices.why: A model predicts or decides; a repeated measurement is a BI job.

choices.text: It is dropped, since an analysis is done once
choices.why: Being needed again is exactly the signal to keep it, defined.

choices.text: It moves to the BI side and gets a written definition
choices.why: Right: a recurring answer needs to be measured the same way each time.

choices.text: The data engineer automates it into a pipeline and owns it from then on
choices.why: The engineer moves data; deciding what the number means is not his job.

prompt: The data engineer answers whether the data arrived complete and on time; when the answer is yes, ___ notices, which is why the role is easy to underrate.
hint: A success that is invisible.

prompt: Put the four parts of Renata's question in the order the work had to happen at Varanda.
hint: Nothing can be counted before a customer can be recognised twice.
items: Build a customer table linking each order to its account
Count how many 2025 first-time customers came back, and look for differences
Write the definition of the repeat rate and report it monthly
Score each customer's chance of returning with a model
trap: The model is what Renata asked for, but it is the last step and Varanda has nobody to build it yet.

prompt: 41,200 customers placed their first online order in the first half of 2025, and 11,900 of them ordered again within 180 days. What is the repeat rate, in percent to one decimal?
hint: Came back divided by first-time customers.

prompt: Renata's repeat rate was computed the same way during the exploration and in the monthly report. What, by the lesson, made the second one BI?
hint: Not the calculation.

choices.text: It was moved into a BI tool
choices.why: The tool is not what BI is; the lesson names the definition and the repetition.

choices.text: Renata, a director, asked for it
choices.why: She asked for the exploration too; who asks does not change the kind of work.

choices.text: It used a larger sample of customers than the exploration had
choices.why: The data was the same; nothing in the lesson changes its size.

choices.text: A written definition that does not move, and repetition
choices.why: Right: who counts, what "again" means, why 180 days — written once and used every month.

prompt: Varanda has no data scientist, and Renata wants to know which individual customers will come back. Which response does the lesson present as the honest one?
hint: A rule Lívia can defend, and a model only if it beats it.

choices.text: Say that no model is available yet, and offer a simple targeting rule backed by the data
choices.why: Right: on-time first orders came back more (29.4% against 21.9%), so target that group and test.

choices.text: Rank customers by how much they spent, and call it a prediction
choices.why: Calling a sort a prediction is claiming a model nobody built.

choices.text: Wait until Varanda hires a data scientist
choices.why: The campaign is in May; a defensible simple answer now beats none.

choices.text: Send the campaign to every customer who ever bought, since nobody can tell them apart
choices.why: The data does tell two groups apart; ignoring it throws the analysis away.

prompt: Why did Tiago's first customer table cover the online shop only?
hint: How does a till know who paid?

choices.text: The stores sell too little to matter
choices.why: The nine stores sell most of Varanda's R$ 98.0 million.

choices.text: Online orders belong to accounts; at the tills customers are mostly anonymous
choices.why: Right: a customer the data cannot recognise twice cannot be counted as returning.

choices.text: Renata asked for the online shop only
choices.why: The campaign was online, but the reason given is what the data can recognise.

choices.text: Store data is personal data and the online data is not
choices.why: An online account holds more personal data, not less.

prompt: An advert is titled "Data Analyst" and asks you to define KPIs, build and maintain dashboards and gather requirements from managers. By the lesson, what job is it?
hint: Read the verbs, not the title.

choices.text: A data analyst job, as the title says
choices.why: The title is a hint; the verbs are the evidence, and they describe recurring reporting.

choices.text: A BI job under another title
choices.why: Right: KPIs, maintained dashboards and requirements are the BI analyst's verbs.

choices.text: A data engineering job, because dashboards need pipelines
choices.why: Nothing in that list asks for pipelines.

choices.text: A trick: the company does not know what it wants
choices.why: The lesson says it is not a trick; it is the company using the market's words.

prompt: Match each phrase from a job advert to the role it points at.
hint: The verbs sort it.

pairs.left: Investigate ad hoc questions from the board
Train and deploy a churn model

prompt: Lívia does BI, exploration and sometimes engineering. Why does the lesson say it matters that she knows which one she is doing?
hint: A rough exploration, a monthly number.

choices.text: Each hat is billed to a different department
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson is about billing.

choices.text: She is allowed only one of them by her contract
choices.why: The lesson calls doing three of them normal at Varanda's size.

choices.text: Each is held to a different standard
choices.why: Right: an exploration can be rough; a number shown every month needs a fixed definition.

choices.text: So she can hand the engineering back to Tiago straight away
choices.why: She fixed pipelines because Tiago works three days a week; handing back is not the point.

prompt: The analytics ___ turns delivered data into clean, tested, documented tables where "a sale" is defined once, in code, for every report.
hint: A newer title, between two of the four.

prompt: After cancelled orders left the data, 1,400 of the 41,200 first-time customers disappeared and 11,900 still came back. What did the repeat rate become, in percent to one decimal?
hint: The numerator did not change; the denominator did.

prompt: The repeat rate rose a full point on 1 March with no customer behaving differently. What was the problem, by the lesson?
hint: Both definitions were defensible.

choices.text: Tiago made a mistake in the pipeline
choices.why: The change was good and asked for by finance; nothing in it was a mistake.

choices.text: Excluding cancelled orders is always wrong
choices.why: Both definitions are defensible; the lesson does not prefer one.

choices.text: One definition replaced the other and nobody downstream was ever told
choices.why: Right: the change was fine; the missing change notice made the number lie.

choices.text: The campaign team really did improve repeat purchases that month
choices.why: That was Renata's guess, and it is the misreading the change caused.

prompt: Two reports at Varanda show different sales for the same month. Which of these does the lesson list as common causes? Choose all that apply.
hint: Three causes.

choices.text: Each counts a sale at a different moment, invoiced or ordered
choices.why: Right: two definitions, both right for their purpose.

choices.text: One reads the database, the other a spreadsheet exported in January
choices.why: Right: two copies drift apart.

choices.text: One of them uses a different BI tool
choices.why: Two tools reading the same data with the same definition agree.

choices.text: A source changed and only the reports built on it moved
choices.why: Right: the silent upstream change, as in March.

prompt: Who does the lesson say should own the definition of the repeat rate?
hint: The person who acts on it.

choices.text: Tiago, because the data passes through his pipeline
choices.why: The engineer moves data and should not decide what a returning customer is.

choices.text: Lívia, because she computes it
choices.why: She keeps the written definition; owning it means deciding, which belongs to whoever acts.

choices.text: Renata, with Lívia keeping the written definition
choices.why: Right: the owner decides what it means and is told before it changes.

choices.text: Nobody in particular; whoever last changed the code
choices.why: That is what the lesson says happens when a number has no owner, and why it needs one.

prompt: Match each artefact to what it says.
hint: Four things that cross a handoff.

pairs.right: What is counted and excluded, over what period
What each column means and where it comes from
What changes, from when, and which numbers will move
What one team promises to deliver to another

prompt: Caio asks Lívia for a system that tells each warehouse picker which order to pack next, updated every minute. Which role does that request describe?
hint: Does it report, explore, or decide on its own?

choices.text: A BI analyst, since it is shown on a screen every day
choices.why: Appearing on a screen is not the test; it chooses an action for each case.

choices.text: A data analyst, since the question is new
choices.why: The question is new, but the deliverable is a running decision, not an answer once.

choices.text: A data scientist, since it decides case by case
choices.why: Right: something that decides on its own for each order is a model, whatever the screen looks like.

choices.text: Nobody: warehouse work is operations, not data
choices.why: Operations is where decisions happen; the role is defined by what is delivered.

prompt: Tiago plans to stop loading orders from a discontinued payment method next month. By this lesson, what should happen before he does? Choose all that apply.
hint: The March surprise, avoided.

choices.text: A change notice saying what changes, from when, and which numbers move
choices.why: Right: that is the artefact whose absence moved the repeat rate.

choices.text: The owners of the affected numbers are told before it happens
choices.why: Right: an owner is told before a number changes.

choices.text: Lívia adjusts her reports afterwards so the totals look the same as before
choices.why: Adjusting a number to hide a change is what the lesson says not to do.

choices.text: Tiago decides alone, since pipelines are his
choices.why: The pipeline is his; what the numbers mean belongs to their owners.
